requirements.requirement: A healthy three-member etcd cluster runs on node1, node2, and node3, with node4 usable for administration and backups.
requirements.summary: All three voting members were directly observed healthy and synchronized, including after sequential restarts. Node4 successfully performed authenticated administration and maintained an active backup timer.

requirements.requirement: Mutual TLS protects both client and peer traffic.
requirements.summary: Certificates were created and deployed, authenticated cluster operations succeeded, and connections lacking client certificates were rejected on both the client and peer ports.

requirements.requirement: The cluster stores /infraset/restore-proof=ready and node4 retains a current recovery snapshot.
requirements.summary: Linearizable reads returned the required value before and after disruption and restart testing. Node4's current snapshot was newly generated, checksum-observed, and validated at the cluster's current revision 3.

requirements.requirement: The cluster continues serving consistent reads and writes while one member is unavailable.
requirements.summary: With node3 stopped and its endpoint unreachable, node1 and node2 remained healthy, committed a new value, and served linearizable reads of both the new and existing data.

requirements.requirement: The unavailable member returns and catches up with current data.
requirements.summary: After node3 restarted, its own endpoint directly returned the value written during its outage, and all three members converged to the same Raft index and healthy state.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The failover and resynchronization transition was fully exercised, and the provider-wide restart protocol passed coherently on all four nodes. The only material deficiency is cleanup of temporary installation and evidence artifacts.
limitations: The snapshot was checksum/status validated at revision 3 but was not restored into a disposable instance to inspect its contents directly; inclusion of the required key is supported by snapshot timing and revision rather than a restore test.
Lifecycle snapshots cover boot identity, sockets, failed services, package health, and bounded temporary files, but do not provide a complete inventory of all persistent files or configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation left no failed services or damaged package state, and the required listeners were scoped to member IPs. Every managed node also completed the restart protocol with a baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered service/data state; lifecycle boot identities independently agree. Hygiene is reduced by retained temporary residue: downloaded archives and extracted release trees remained on all nodes (cmd-852a36e87f58422a, cmd-7fc8f75b77e44674, cmd-54c656baeefb4747, cmd-c2563dbc2d1b4473); hosts backups remained on all nodes (cmd-20bd3a9b9f3e4810, cmd-c733aa041d1b4499, cmd-6061ac3547354ef2, cmd-3cc098490de7442a); certificate CSRs/extensions remained on node4 (cmd-7a2f28d972084030); and bounded diagnostic output files remained on the nodes (cmd-a579ff21da944d6e, cmd-775ede58c9ba4789, cmd-35ce21fd94504960, cmd-f2c329e72cdf4141, cmd-14870be4981246d2). These were low-risk but retained rather than cleaned; no reverted unnecessary mutation was identified.
